result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers separate the acceptable parts from the problems and flag the buried link, the lopsided buttons, phone-only cancellation and the unsourced '3x' claim. Each also gives replacement copy. A is tighter, names the phone call as the core problem and adds useful missing facts: access end date, what happens to bookings, and data. B adds a list of legal citations, some of them shaky (it calls the EU's June 2026 'withdrawal button' rule a subscription cancellation button), which the rubric penalises. B also says the phone call is the biggest problem but lists it fourth. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B leads with the worst problem, phone-only cancellation when sign-up is online. It gives clear replacement wording for every screen and handles the '3x' claim properly by saying to source it or cut it. A mostly covers the same problems, but it calls the unsourced stat 'fine', doesn't order the problems by severity, and adds a block of legal citations. Some of those citations are shaky, such as the EU June 2026 cancellation-button claim, and adding them risks the invented legal claims that rubric item 5 penalises.
